note: ApiHandlerRole.secretsmanager:GetSecretValue Resource is intentionally set to '*' in this scenario (rather than !Ref DbSecret) so that the IAM check passes and the ResourceNotFoundException from Secrets Manager is the observable symptom — making it distinct from fault12 (AccessDeniedException).
valid_fixes: Restore ApiHandlerFunction env DB_SECRET_ARN to !Ref DbSecret so the Lambda references the real deployed secret
invalid_patches: Create a new secret at the wrong ARN path to match the bad reference
Grant secretsmanager:* on * to work around the scope
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_get_log_tail(ace-bench-stack-api-handler) → shows ResourceNotFoundException on the secret ARN
ace_get_environment_variables(ace-bench-stack-api-handler) → reveals DB_SECRET_ARN points to a nonexistent ARN
ace_get_stack_outputs(ace-bench-stack) → shows real DbSecretArn; comparing to env var confirms the ARN mismatch
observability_check: functional_test assertion 'order_created' (POST /orders returns 201) fails; Lambda logs show ResourceNotFoundException for the wrong secret ARN
observable_symptom: POST /orders returns 500 on every request. Lambda logs show a ResourceNotFoundException when attempting to retrieve the database credentials — the secret ARN in the Lambda environment does not correspond to any existing secret. The IAM role has correct GetSecretValue permissions and a valid secret with correct credentials does exist in the account.
root_cause: The Lambda function's DB_SECRET_ARN environment variable points to a nonexistent secret ARN ('ace-bench-stack-db-secret-wrong') instead of the actual deployed secret. Secrets Manager raises ResourceNotFoundException on every invocation before a database connection is attempted.
